content.value_statement: Disconnected asset, finance, and rights records create reconciliation and audit gaps. This skill designs linked ledgers, asset cards, controls, and operating procedures.
actual_capabilities: Designs asset, finance, and rights ledgers with defined relationships.
Creates data asset cards covering identity, ownership, technology, finance, security, and responsibility.
Defines unique asset numbering rules and shared master data principles.
Produces reconciliation and inventory workflows with documented review records.
Structures annual impairment reviews around operational, technical, legal, and usage indicators.
Drafts ledger governance procedures, quality checks, responsibilities, and handover controls.
limitations: Does not connect directly to finance, registry, or data management systems.
Cannot verify supplied ownership evidence, balances, valuations, or source records.
Does not replace licensed accounting, valuation, audit, or legal advice.
Policy references and timing recommendations require review against current local requirements.

use_cases.title: Create a First Ledger
use_cases.description: Turn an approved data asset list into linked ledgers, asset cards, numbering rules, and ownership fields.

use_cases.title: Resolve Ledger Differences
use_cases.description: Analyze missing, retired, or differently classified assets and define a repeatable reconciliation process.

use_cases.title: Prepare Audit Evidence
use_cases.description: Organize inventory records, responsibility assignments, amortization data, impairment reviews, and supporting evidence indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Asset Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a data asset card for [asset name]. Include identity, ownership, technical, financial, security, responsibility, and status fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a complete record for one asset.

prompt_templates.title: Design Three Ledgers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design asset, finance, and rights ledgers for [organization]. Define shared identifiers, required fields, owners, update events, and reconciliation points.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is establishing its ledger structure.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Reconciliation Gap
prompt_templates.prompt: Our asset ledger has [count] items, while finance has [count]. Classify likely causes and provide investigation steps, evidence needs, and controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Finance and operations report different asset populations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Governance Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a governance program for [portfolio]. Include initialization, system integration, access control, quarterly reconciliation, inventory, impairment review, reporting, and handover.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs an end-to-end operating model.

output_examples.input: Design a card for a customer behavior dataset.
output_examples.output: Asset card sections: identity and classification; source and rights; scale and storage; cost and amortization; quality and security; owner and status.

output_examples.input: Explain why 20 assets are missing from the finance ledger.
output_examples.output: Investigation plan: compare identifiers, approval status, recognition criteria, disposal records, posting dates, and classification. Record each difference, owner, evidence, action, and due date.
Review each asset for declining relevance, lost use cases, technical replacement, legal restrictions, and reduced recoverable value. Document evidence, assumptions, approval, and accounting action.

best_practices: Use one stable identifier across asset, finance, rights, and supporting systems.
Keep evidence links, accountable owners, review dates, and approvals for every material change.
Reconcile ledgers regularly and resolve differences through documented ownership and deadlines.
anti_patterns: Do not create separate identifiers or uncontrolled copies for each system.
Do not record values or ownership conclusions without supporting evidence and stated assumptions.
Do not postpone inventory or impairment review until an audit request arrives.

faq.question: What are the three ledgers?
faq.answer: They are the asset ledger, finance ledger, and rights ledger. Shared identifiers connect operational, accounting, and ownership information.

faq.question: What belongs on a data asset card?
faq.answer: Include identity, source, rights, technical scale, financial data, quality, security, responsibility, status, and review dates.

faq.question: Can this skill update our systems?
faq.answer: No. It designs structures and procedures but does not connect to or modify external systems.

faq.question: How often should ledgers be reconciled?
faq.answer: The knowledge base proposes regular finance reconciliation and periodic inventory. Confirm the final schedule with organizational and regulatory requirements.

faq.question: Does it provide a formal valuation?
faq.answer: No. It can organize inputs and controls, but licensed professionals must approve valuations and accounting conclusions.

faq.question: Can it support audit preparation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure evidence indexes, reconciliation records, inventory results, impairment reviews, responsibilities, and change histories.
